meta.title: Cymbal Shop on Google Cloud: Serverless Web Application with Cloud Run
meta.subtitle: Reference Architecture
meta.description: Customers reach Cloud Run services through a global external HTTPS load balancer with Cloud Armor and Cloud CDN. The services reach Cloud SQL and Memorystore on private IPs through a Serverless VPC Access connector, keep credentials in Secret Manager, serve static assets from Cloud Storage, and expose an admin console only through Identity-Aware Proxy. Adapted from the Google Cloud Architecture Center's guidance for serverless web applications, set at Google's sample organization Cymbal.
meta.author: DigitalPrez, LLC
meta.objective: Run the storefront without servers to manage, with every data store on a private IP, every credential in Secret Manager and every administrative page behind Identity-Aware Proxy.
meta.flow_summary: Customer to the storefront; API to Cloud SQL, Memorystore and Secret Manager; SRE to the admin console through IAP
meta.access_summary: Customers: Identity Platform with MFA (OIDC). SREs: Cloud Identity with a security key, then IAP. Services: per-service accounts, ID tokens between services, no key files.
assumptions: One production project with Org Policy constraints applied at the folder
Cloud Run ingress is restricted to the load balancer and the VPC
Cloud SQL and Memorystore have private IPs only, through Private Service Access
out_of_scope: The Cloud Build pipeline that builds and deploys the images
BigQuery analytics fed from Cloud SQL exports

auth_types.label: Identity Platform + MFA (OIDC)
auth_types.description: Customer sign-in through Identity Platform with MFA; the storefront receives OIDC tokens.

auth_types.label: Ingress: Load Balancer Only
auth_types.description: Cloud Run accepts requests only from the load balancer and the VPC; the request carries no caller identity of its own.

auth_types.label: Service Account ID Token
auth_types.description: Service-to-service calls carry a Google-signed ID token; the callee's IAM policy admits only the caller's service account.

auth_types.label: Service Account (IAM)
auth_types.description: The workload identity of the Cloud Run service; no key file anywhere.

auth_types.label: Cloud SQL IAM Authentication + TLS
auth_types.description: Database sign-in with the service account over TLS; no database password in the application.

auth_types.label: Memorystore AUTH String
auth_types.description: A shared AUTH string in the service's configuration; no identity, no rotation.

auth_types.label: Signed URL
auth_types.description: Time-limited signed URLs for uploads, minted by the storefront with its service account.

auth_types.label: Cloud Identity + Security Key
auth_types.description: Workforce sign-in with a FIDO2 security key enforced by Cloud Identity.

auth_types.label: Identity-Aware Proxy (OIDC)
auth_types.description: IAP checks the identity, the access level and the device before the request reaches the service.

auth_types.label: IAP-Signed JWT
auth_types.description: The admin service verifies the signed IAP header on every request, so a bypass of the proxy carries no valid identity.

zones.name: gcp-project
zones.label: Google Cloud Project: Cymbal-Shop-Prod
zones.info: One production project under the Cymbal organization. Org Policy enforces public access prevention, uniform bucket-level access and domain-restricted sharing.

zones.info: Fully managed Cloud Run services; each runs as its own service account and reaches the VPC through the connector.

zones.name: vpc-prod
zones.label: Production VPC
zones.info: Holds the connector subnet and the Private Service Access range for Cloud SQL and Memorystore. No workload has a public IP.

appliances.name: fw-rules
appliances.label: VPC Firewall
appliances.info: Firewall rules admit the connector range to the database and cache ports; everything else is denied by the implied rule.

zones.name: snet-connector
zones.label: Connector Subnet
zones.info: Dedicated /28 for the Serverless VPC Access connector instances.

zones.name: snet-services
zones.label: Private Services Range
zones.info: Google-managed range peered into the VPC; Cloud SQL and Memorystore answer here on private IPs only.

zones.name: gcp-services
zones.label: Google Cloud APIs
zones.sub: IAP · Secret Manager · Logging · Cloud Storage
zones.info: Regional Google APIs the services call with their service accounts over Private Google Access; a VPC Service Controls perimeter around the project keeps the data from leaving it.

appliances.name: vpc-sc
appliances.label: VPC Service Controls
appliances.info: A service perimeter around the project: Secret Manager and Cloud Storage API calls from outside the perimeter are denied even with valid credentials.

steps.name: request
steps.title: A customer reaches the storefront through the global load balancer
steps.description: The customer's browser resolves the storefront name to the load balancer's anycast IP. Cloud Armor applies preconfigured WAF rules and a rate limit before anything reaches a Cloud Run service; static assets come from Cloud CDN.
details: One public entry point for the whole application
Cloud Armor WAF rules and rate limiting
Managed TLS certificates, TLS 1.2 or later

steps.name: signin
steps.title: The customer signs in through Identity Platform
steps.description: Identity Platform issues OIDC tokens after MFA; the storefront carries the token on every request and validates it.
details: MFA and reCAPTCHA Enterprise on sign-in
Tokens validated by the storefront service

steps.name: storefront
steps.title: The load balancer forwards to the storefront service
steps.description: A serverless network endpoint group routes to the storefront on Cloud Run. Ingress is restricted to the load balancer and the VPC, so the run.app URL answers 403 to anyone else.
details: Ingress: internal and Cloud Load Balancing
No unauthenticated invocation

steps.name: orders
steps.title: The storefront calls the Orders API, which reaches Cloud SQL through the VPC connector
steps.description: The storefront presents an ID token; the API, invoked only by that service account, reaches the database on its private IP through the Serverless VPC Access connector with IAM database authentication.
details: ID tokens between services
Private IP, IAM authentication, TLS
Firewall: connector range only

steps.name: cache-secrets
steps.title: The API reads the cache and its secrets
steps.description: Session and catalogue reads go to Memorystore with the shared AUTH string; API keys and the AUTH string itself come from Secret Manager inside the VPC Service Controls perimeter.
details: Memorystore: AUTH string, in-transit encryption
Secret Manager inside the perimeter

steps.name: assets
steps.title: Static assets come from Cloud Storage through Cloud CDN; uploads use signed URLs
steps.description: The load balancer serves the assets prefix from a backend bucket; the storefront mints signed URLs so customers upload documents straight to the bucket. Public access prevention is enforced by Org Policy.
details: Public access prevention, uniform bucket-level access
Customer-managed encryption key

steps.name: operate
steps.title: Every service logs to Cloud Logging; findings reach the on-call SRE
steps.description: Request logs, audit logs and data-access logs are collected with alerting; Security Command Center findings page the on-call rotation.
details: Data-access audit logs for Cloud SQL and Secret Manager
Security Command Center findings to on-call

steps.name: admin
steps.title: An SRE opens the admin console through Identity-Aware Proxy
steps.description: The SRE signs in to Cloud Identity with a security key; IAP checks the identity, the access level and the device, then forwards the request with a signed header that the admin service verifies. Changes go through the same Orders API.
details: Security key required
Context-aware access: managed devices only
IAP JWT verified in the service

steps.name: denied
steps.title: What the attacker cannot do
steps.description: Direct calls to the run.app URLs and public reads of the bucket are refused before any application code runs; the admin console answers only to IAP, and Cloud SQL and Memorystore have no public IP at all.
details: Cloud Run: ingress restricted, no unauthenticated invocation
Admin console: IAP only
Cloud SQL and Memorystore: private IP only
Cloud Storage: public access prevention
steps.outcome: The public surface is the load balancer and nothing else.

threats.title: Credential Stuffing Against Identity Platform Sign-In
threats.description: Password lists replayed against the hosted sign-in endpoint from rotating IP ranges.

attack.scenario: Automated sign-in attempts; successful pairs are resold or used for fraudulent orders.

risk.rationale: Hosted sign-in is public; a taken-over account exposes PII and payment references.
risk.consequence: An attacker holds a valid customer session and can read and change that customer's orders.

residual.rationale: MFA and reCAPTCHA Enterprise (CTL-0001) stop matched passwords; Cloud Armor rate limiting (CTL-0002) throttles the campaign.

provenance.notes: Illustrative example for the reference architecture.

threats.title: Direct Calls to the Run.app URL Bypass Cloud Armor
threats.description: Every Cloud Run service has a run.app URL. If ingress allowed all traffic, an attacker could reach the storefront and the API without passing the load balancer, Cloud Armor or the rate limit.

attack.scenario: The run.app URL is guessed or found in a client bundle; injection payloads go to it directly.

risk.rationale: run.app URLs are predictable; without the ingress setting every Cloud Armor rule is moot.
risk.consequence: Injection and brute-force traffic reaches the services unfiltered.

residual.rationale: Ingress is internal-and-load-balancing and invocation requires IAM (CTL-0003); the URL answers 403.

provenance.notes: Illustrative example for the reference architecture.

threats.title: Compromised Dependency in the Orders API Runs with the Service Account
threats.description: A poisoned package in the API image runs at startup with the identity and the network reach of the service: Secret Manager, the VPC connector and unrestricted Internet egress.

attack.scenario: A typosquatted or hijacked npm package is pulled into the API image; its postinstall script fetches a payload that runs with the service account.

risk.rationale: Package compromises are regular news; the service identity opens the data layer.
risk.consequence: Code of an attacker's choosing runs with the API's identity and network reach.

residual.rationale: Artifact Analysis scanning (CTL-0005) catches known vulnerable versions, not a fresh malicious release.

projected.rationale: Binary Authorization (CTL-0004) admits only images attested by the pipeline from a pinned, reviewed lockfile.

suggested_mitigations.text: Set VPC egress to "all traffic" through the connector and Cloud NAT with a Cloud NGFW egress policy, so a compromised service cannot reach arbitrary Internet hosts.

provenance.notes: Illustrative example for the reference architecture.

threats.title: Shared AUTH String Gives Any VPC Workload Full Access to the Cache
threats.description: Memorystore authenticates with one AUTH string held in Secret Manager and in every service that uses the cache. Anything that reaches the private IP with the string reads every session and cached record.

attack.scenario: A workload compromised anywhere in the VPC reads the AUTH string from its environment or from Secret Manager and connects to the cache.

risk.rationale: Shared secrets spread; the cache holds live sessions.
risk.consequence: Session hijack and bulk read of cached customer data.

residual.rationale: The firewall admits only the connector range (CTL-0009); the string itself still grants everything.

projected.rationale: IAM authentication for Memorystore with per-service identities and TLS (CTL-0006) replaces the shared string.

suggested_mitigations.text: Enable IAM authentication on the Memorystore instance, grant redis.dbConnectionUser per service account and remove the AUTH string from Secret Manager.

provenance.notes: Illustrative example for the reference architecture.

threats.title: One Service Account for Every Service Reads Every Secret and Opens the Database
threats.description: The three Cloud Run services run as one service account with Secret Manager Accessor on the whole project and Cloud SQL Client. Any one of them, compromised, inherits the reach of all three.

attack.scenario: Code running in any service lists and reads every secret in the project and connects to Cloud SQL with the shared identity.

risk.rationale: One shared identity turns any foothold into full data access.
risk.consequence: Any compromise of a service is a compromise of the whole data layer.

residual.rationale: Data-access audit logs and Security Command Center (CTL-0011) show unusual secret reads after the fact; nothing prevents them.

projected.rationale: Per-service accounts with per-secret bindings and a least-privilege database role (CTL-0007) limit each service to what it uses.

suggested_mitigations.text: Create one service account per Cloud Run service, bind Secret Manager Accessor on individual secrets only, and give the storefront no database role at all.

provenance.notes: Illustrative example for the reference architecture.

threats.title: Bucket Misconfiguration Exposes Customer Uploads to the Internet
threats.description: An allUsers grant on the uploads prefix, added for a support case, would make customer documents readable by anyone with the URL.

attack.scenario: Bucket scanners enumerate names and copy everything listable within hours of a public grant.

risk.rationale: Org Policy makes the grant impossible rather than merely unlikely.
risk.consequence: Customer documents readable by anyone with the URL.

residual.rationale: Public access prevention is enforced at the organization and uniform bucket-level access removes object ACLs (CTL-0008).

provenance.notes: Illustrative example for the reference architecture.

requirements.title: Customer Data Reachable Only Over Private IP
requirements.statement: Cloud SQL and Memorystore have no public address; only the Serverless VPC Access connector range may reach their ports, over TLS with IAM authentication.

requirements.title: Only Attested Images Run in Production
requirements.statement: Every Cloud Run revision is built by the pipeline, scanned by Artifact Analysis and admitted by Binary Authorization; an image from anywhere else is refused.

attack_paths.title: Dependency Compromise to Secrets to Customer Data
attack_paths.description: A poisoned package runs in the Orders API with the shared service account; the account reads every secret; the database is read through the connector; the data leaves through the service's own Internet egress.

hops.note: A hijacked npm package pulled into the Orders API image runs its payload at container start, with the API's service account and network reach.
The shared service account holds Secret Manager Accessor on the whole project: API keys, the Redis AUTH string and the Cloud SQL built-in user password are one call each.
With the built-in user password and Cloud SQL Client, the payload dumps the orders tables through the connector; the firewall sees the connector range as usual.
Cloud Run egress for public ranges goes straight to the Internet; the dump is posted to an attacker-controlled host from inside the service.

attack_paths.impact: Customer orders, PII and payment references copied out of the project: regulatory notification, card-brand exposure and a rotation of every secret in the project.

risk.rationale: Package compromises are regular; the shared identity and open egress let one of them run to completion.

residual.rationale: Scanning (CTL-0005) and audit logs (CTL-0011) shorten the dwell time; nothing breaks the chain today.

projected.rationale: Binary Authorization (CTL-0004) stops hop 1 and per-service accounts with per-secret bindings (CTL-0007) stop hop 2.
